machine: darwin arm64, node v22.22.0, Apple M4

summary.via: openai writer (callOpenAI) through OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible API, model anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5, the request exactly as this build sends it

rows.input: I tried switching the file watcher to the notify crate's poll backend to fix the missed events on NFS home dirs. It pegs a core at 100% with 20k files, so I backed it out.
rows.line: Tried notify crate poll backend to fix NFS home dir missed events, but it caused 100% CPU on single core with 20k files, so reverted it.

rows.input: fyi I tried next/image with the Cloudflare loader for the condition photos. it broke on the preview deployments because the loader needs the zone to be proxied and previews aren't. reverted to the default loader.
rows.line: Next/image with Cloudflare loader for condition photos failed on preview deployments because loader requires proxied zone; reverted to default loader.

rows.input: Polars was my first try for the Parquet conversion, but it chokes on the nested sensor arrays from the older buoys (list of struct with nulls), so the DAG stays on pyarrow.
rows.line: Polars failed for Parquet conversion due to choking on nested sensor arrays (list of struct with nulls) from older buoys; DAG uses pyarrow instead.

rows.input: We already tried moving driver locations to Postgres with PostGIS last spring. The nearest-driver query took ~40 ms at peak, which blows the budget once the pricing call is added, so we went back to Redis GEO.
rows.line: Moved driver locations to Postgres/PostGIS last spring but nearest-driver queries took ~40ms at peak, exceeding budget with pricing call overhead, reverted to Redis GEO.

rows.input: Tried Isar instead of drift for the inspection records. Its migrations can't rename a field without copying every object, and some devices have 200k records. Not worth it, dropping it.
rows.line: Isar migrations can't rename fields without copying all objects; impractical with 200k+ records per device; switched back to drift.

rows.input: tried Stripe Tax's automatic mode for EU orders last week. it charged VAT on used books in Ireland where books are zero-rated, and support says the product tax code can't be overridden per item in Checkout. turned it off again.
rows.line: Stripe Tax automatic mode overcharged VAT on zero-rated Irish books; product tax codes can't be overridden per item in Checkout, so disabled it.

rows.input: The git2 crate was a dead end for pushing: it can't use SSH keys held by the 1Password agent, so every push failed for people on 1Password. We shell out to the git binary now.
rows.line: Git2 crate couldn't authenticate with 1Password SSH agent so pushes failed; switched to shelling out to git binary instead.

rows.input: we attempted to trigger the DAG from Airflow datasets instead of the nightly cron, but the S3 events arrive one per file and it kicked off the DAG about 3,000 times a night. back to cron.
rows.line: Airflow dataset-based DAG triggering from S3 events failed because each file generates a separate event, causing ~3,000 DAG runs per night; reverted to nightly cron schedule.

rows.input: I prototyped the matcher with an in-memory k-d tree to skip the Redis round trip. Lookups were fast, but rebuilding the tree on every location update cost more than the round trip it saved. Shelved.
rows.line: In-memory k-d tree matcher prototype failed because rebuild cost on each location update exceeded Redis round trip savings; shelved in favor of Redis approach.

rows.input: I tried rayon's par_bridge over walkdir, but the order of the diff output became nondeterministic and two snapshot tests broke; sorting afterwards ate the gain (1.9 s against 2.1 s). I reverted it, so scan is still single-threaded.
rows.line: Rayon par_bridge over walkdir was dropped because it made diff output nondeterministic, breaking snapshot tests; sorting results negated perf gain (1.9s vs 2.1s), so scan remains single-threaded.

rows.input: I tried pushing the QC flag filter down into the pyarrow scan with a dataset filter expression, but the flag column is stored as strings in the 2019–2021 partitions, so the pushdown silently matched nothing there. I backed that out; the Python-side filter stays until those partitions are rewritten.
rows.line: QC flag filter pushdown to pyarrow scan was dropped because flag column is string-typed in 2019-2021 partitions, causing silent mismatches; Python-side filter retained

rows.input: I tried client keepalive at 10 s. Pricing's server enforces a 5-minute minimum and answered with GOAWAY too_many_pings, which dropped in-flight calls, so I removed it. The spikes need a different fix.
rows.line: Client keepalive at 10s failed: pricing server enforces 5min minimum, returns GOAWAY too_many_pings, dropped calls; removed it; need different approach for spikes.

rows.input: I enabled Impeller on Android, but the inspection map's custom shader rendered black on the Samsung A-series tablets the field teams use (Mali GPUs). I switched it back off for Android; iOS keeps it.
rows.line: Impeller on Android with Mali GPUs caused custom shaders in inspection map to render black; disabled for Android only, kept on iOS.

rows.input: I tried the global singleton pattern together with Prisma Accelerate's connection pooling. The cold start stayed at about 1.1 s, because most of it is the query engine binary loading, not the connection. I removed Accelerate again to avoid the extra bill.
rows.line: Global singleton pattern with Prisma Accelerate didn't reduce cold start (stayed ~1.1s) because query engine binary loading dominates, not connection time; removed Accelerate to avoid extra costs.

rows.input: I tried the temp-dir-and-rename approach, but rename(2) across mounts fails with EXDEV, and on a read-only mount the target directory can't be written at all, so there is no way around it. Apply is unchanged; it now reports read-only targets before it starts.
rows.line: Temp-dir-and-rename approach failed due to EXDEV errors on cross-mount renames and inability to write target on read-only mounts; Apply now reports read-only targets upfront instead.

rows.input: I tried wrapping the checklist in a ListView.builder with const item widgets, but each item still rebuilt on every keystroke because they all watch the same form provider; frame times stayed around 45 ms. I reverted it. The fix will need per-item providers, which is a bigger change, so I left a note in the issue.
rows.line: ListView.builder with const items didn't prevent rebuilds (45ms frame time) because all items watched same form provider; reverted; per-item providers needed as bigger refactor.

rows.input: Background fetch for the photo outbox was a no-go: iOS gave us at most one run every few hours, so photos sat on the phone all shift. We went with uploading in the foreground whenever the app is open.
rows.line: Background fetch for photo outbox failed on iOS—rate-limited to ~1 execution per few hours, photos stuck queued during shifts; switched to foreground upload when app is open.

rows.input: I tried generateStaticParams for all 48k listings; the build hit Vercel's 45-minute limit at about 30k pages. I dropped full static generation and made the product pages ISR with a one-hour revalidate instead.
rows.line: GenerateStaticParams for 48k listings hit Vercel 45-minute build limit at ~30k pages; switched to ISR with revalidate=3600 for product pages instead.

rows.input: The p99 spikes are back. I first tried bumping GOGC to 200, no change at all. Setting GOMEMLIMIT to 1.5 GiB did fix it, p99 is back under 120 ms.
rows.line: GOGC=200 didn't reduce p99 spikes; GOMEMLIMIT=1.5GiB fixed them under 120ms

rows.input: Creating symlinks on Windows needs Developer Mode or an elevated process. I first tried turning Developer Mode on in the runner through the registry, but the windows-2022 image blocks that key. Running the symlink tests in an elevated pwsh step works, so the job does that now.
rows.line: Symlink tests on windows-2022 image fail when enabling Developer Mode via registry (key blocked), but pass when run in elevated pwsh step, which is the current approach.

rows.input: switching the S3 listing to boto3's paginator didn't help with the throttling, SlowDown errors kept coming at about 3.5k requests/s. adding a random prefix to the raw keys spread the load and they're gone.
rows.line: Switching the S3 listing to boto3's paginator didn't help with the throttling, SlowDown errors kept coming at about 3.5k requests/s.

rows.input: Stripe webhooks were getting 504s. Raising the function timeout to 60 s didn't help, still 504 because the handler waits on the POS sync. Moving the POS sync to a queue and acking the webhook straight away fixed it.
rows.line: Stripe webhooks were getting 504s. Raising the function timeout to 60 s didn't help, still 504 because the handler waits on the POS sync.

rows.input: Crash on older Androids when opening the camera. Pinning the camera plugin to 0.10.5 didn't fix it, same NullPointerException inside CameraX. Using the medium resolution preset below API 29 did.
rows.line: Crashed on older Androids opening camera; pinning camera plugin to 0.10.5 didn't fix NullPointerException in CameraX; resolved by using medium resolution preset below API 29.

rows.input: A Redis WATCH/MULTI transaction around the assignment didn't stop it: both matchers read the same candidate before either one wrote. I switched assignment to a Lua script that checks and sets in one step, and the double-assignment test passes 1,000 out of 1,000 now.
rows.line: Redis WATCH/MULTI transaction around assignment didn't prevent race condition where both matchers read same candidate before either wrote

rows.input: Raising memory_limit to 12 GB only moved the out-of-memory error later; the query keeps an unbounded window over every reading. I rewrote it to aggregate per day first, and it peaks at 1.4 GB now.
rows.line: Raising memory_limit to 12 GB only delayed OOM error; query held unbounded window over all readings; rewriting to aggregate per day first reduced peak to 1.4 GB.

rows.input: We ran DuckDB for the analysts for two months and it's not working: concurrent notebook users lock each other out of the shared .duckdb file, and queries over five years of data take more than 10 minutes. We're moving them to BigQuery.
rows.line: DuckDB with shared .duckdb file caused concurrent notebook user lockouts and slow queries (>10min on 5yr data); switched to BigQuery

rows.input: We gave Riverpod a full sprint and we're done with it: code generation pushed build_runner to 6 minutes on CI and the team kept fighting the generated providers. Back to plain ChangeNotifier with provider.
rows.line: Riverpod abandoned after code generation extended build_runner to 6 minutes on CI and generated providers caused team friction; switched to plain ChangeNotifier with provider.

rows.input: The separate proto repo didn't work out. Every schema change needed two PRs and a tag, and the matcher sat on a stale schema version for weeks. The protos move into this repo under api/.
rows.line: Separate proto repo was dropped due to requiring two PRs per schema change and matcher lagging on stale versions; protos now live in api/ of main repo.

rows.input: We tried to build the bundle discounts on Checkout sessions and hit a wall: a session can't apply a discount that depends on which items are in the cart unless we precompute every combination, and we have 2k bundles. Checkout moves to Payment Elements with our own cart pricing.
rows.line: Tried computing bundle discounts in Checkout sessions but it requires precomputing all 2k bundle combinations; moved pricing logic to Payment Elements with custom cart instead.
